title: How to Avoid Bad Sellers on Fiverr: Red Flags and Checks
h1: How to avoid bad sellers on Fiverr: red flags and checks
description: Red flags to watch for on Fiverr before, during and after an order, and the simple checks that filter out most bad sellers before you pay.
intro: Most Fiverr orders go fine, but a bad one costs time, money and sometimes a deadline. The good news is that most problem sellers show warning signs before you pay. This article lists the red flags worth walking away from and the checks that take only a few minutes.

faq.q: Are new sellers on Fiverr risky?
faq.a: Not necessarily. New sellers can be talented and attentive. Judge them on samples, communication and a small first order rather than on review count alone.

faq.q: Is a very high review count always good?
faq.a: It shows a seller delivers reliably, but check that recent reviews are about work similar to yours.

faq.q: Why shouldn't I pay outside the platform?
faq.a: Payments made outside lose the platform's order record and dispute options, and asking for them breaks Fiverr's rules.

faq.q: What if the delivery is bad?
faq.a: Don't accept it yet. Request a revision with specific feedback. If that fails, contact the seller and then Fiverr's support through the order page.

faq.q: Do badges like Vetted Pro or Top Rated guarantee quality?
faq.a: No badge guarantees a good fit, but they show the seller has a track record or passed a review. Use them to narrow the list, then check samples.
